comment: Rules for `node scripts/test.js --changed`: a changed file is first looked up by its directory (`directoryRules`), then by the file rules below. The first rule whose path prefix matches names the plans to run, as paths under test/plans; a change that no rule matches (or whose plans cannot be found) falls back to the whole fast layer. Directory rules mirror the path under test/plans/feat and take the deepest existing match: modules/tensor/ops.cpp runs the tensor plans, test/cases/compile/enum/x.cml runs feat/compile/enum.plan.toml (not all of feat/compile), test/cases/loops/x.cml falls through to the file rule for loops. Keep the file rules from specific to general: the first match wins. The base branch is origin/develop; CAMEL_TEST_BASE overrides it. Update this file when a subsystem grows a plan of its own; see docs/test-plans.md, 'Selecting plans from a change'.

directoryRules.comment: A test case: its directory is looked up under test/plans/feat (compile, linear, modules/tensor, modules/nn.plan.toml, tools/unicode -> tools, ...).
A module: modules/tensor selects feat/modules/tensor, modules/nn selects feat/modules/nn.plan.toml. A module with no plan of its own (python) falls through to the file rules.
A tool: tools/lsp selects feat/tools/lsp.plan.toml; tools/format falls through to the file rules (feat/format).

rules.comment: The runner itself and the self-test: the plans that exercise the runner and the smoke set.
FastVM and the other schedulers.
Optimization passes.
Any other pass, including the shared pass machinery.
GCT/GIR construction, encoding and the graph printer.
The front end: lexer, parser, AST and diagnostics.
Values, types, the collector and the runtime shell.
Execution, entry arguments and the standalone bridge.
Automatic differentiation.
The ONNX exporter.
Neural-network operators: the nn plan and the plans that train with them.
Tensor operators and shapes.
Keyed random: the random plan and the signatures/reference that list it.
Any other module.
The standard library's Camel sources and signatures.
The language server, debugger, formatter and command-line tools.
Example programs and their recorded output.
Benchmark scripts and artifacts: the slow gradient comparisons and the perf plans.
Documentation checks.
The editor syntax files and their tests.
The build definitions: every backend may be affected, so the smoke set and the runtime plans.
Case directories with no plan directory of their own: their cases are exercised by the module, tool and translation plans.
A case directory with no plan directory of its own: the loop cases are tested by the linear plan.
A case directory with no plan directory of its own: the recursive Fibonacci case is timed by the perf plan.
A plan file selects itself: editing the tests of one plan runs that plan.
